```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4)
has_quanteda <- requireNamespace("quanteda", quietly = TRUE)
```

Topics over Time (TOT; Wang and McCallum, 2006) is a topic model in which
every topic has, besides its distribution over words, a Beta distribution over
continuous time. Topics are therefore found jointly from word co-occurrence and
from *when* documents were written. Time is neither discretized nor modelled
with Markov dynamics, and the meaning of a topic is constant: what changes over
time is how often each topic occurs.

## A simulated corpus

```{r sim}
library(topicovertime)
set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_tot(n_docs = 300, n_topics = 3)
fit <- tot(sim$x, sim$time, k = 3, n_iter = 200)
fit
fit$psi        # Beta parameters on the normalized time scale
plot(fit)      # P(topic | time)
```

## U.S. presidential inaugural addresses

The paper analyses State of the Union addresses; the inaugural addresses
shipped with quanteda are a similar corpus spanning more than two centuries.

```{r inaugural, eval = has_quanteda}
library(quanteda)
toks <- tokens(data_corpus_inaugural, remove_punct = TRUE,
               remove_numbers = TRUE)
toks <- tokens_remove(tokens_tolower(toks), stopwords("en"))
x <- dfm_trim(dfm(toks), min_termfreq = 5)
year <- docvars(data_corpus_inaugural, "Year")

set.seed(2026)
fit <- tot(x, year, k = 8, n_iter = 300)
terms(fit, 8)
plot(fit)
```

`predict()` folds new documents into a fitted model; `type = "time"` predicts
when a document was written:

```{r predict, eval = has_quanteda}
pred <- predict(fit, x, type = "time")
head(data.frame(actual = year, predicted = round(pred)))
cor(pred, year)
```

## Balancing words and time

Each token carries the document's timestamp, so a long document's time
contributes many times to the likelihood. `time_weight` rescales that
contribution: `1` is the sampler exactly as in the paper, and
`"inverse_length"` counts each timestamp once per document. The paper notes
that results are sensitive to this setting and recommends tuning it.

## Reference

Wang, X. and McCallum, A. (2006). Topics over time: a non-Markov
continuous-time model of topical trends. *KDD '06*, 424--433.
<https://doi.org/10.1145/1150402.1150450>
